propositions: Parent-first cascade logic is implemented twice: once in claim.py (hardcoded open parent) and once in transition.py (table-driven _cascade_parent_first), creating duplication and maintenance risk across two write primitives.

The shared walk (ancestor recursion, cycle guard, benign-race TOCTOU re-check, error rewrap preserving ConcurrencyMismatch) must be extracted to a new lifecycle_cascade module while keeping the decision table (_CASCADING_EDGES) at transition.py and the inbound cascade write primitive separate.

All three cascading edges (open→in_progress, closed→open, closed→in_progress) must remain functional after extraction; * → closed must not cascade; reopen must cascade via the (closed→open) row; the cascade=False replay suppression must work unchanged.

Claim supports only one edge (open→in_progress) while transition supports all three; a parametrised test over _CASCADING_EDGES must verify each edge cascades through the real transition surface, with a separate unit test pinning eligible-status contracts per row.
